transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-15 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortega (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (CTO - LakeMed), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Priya Patel (DevOps)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Redwood model catalog UI + API, discussion about selecting open models for triage/chat, review of benchmark numbers and where to run POCs. Action items agreed at end.

[00:00] Sara (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. i'm sara, ae at redwood, i'll kick us off — daniel from our se team is here too. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jared (LakeMed): good, thanks. excited to see what you have. we've been evaluating a couple vendors, want to understand the model choices for our triage assistant and perf expectations.
[00:21] Daniel (Redwood SE): great — today we'll walk through the model catalog in the console, show how benchmarks are surfaced, and then look at our compatibility matrix so you can see which quantized variants and hardware map to latency/cost. we'll also point out workloads where hosted is fine vs where dedicated/private would be recommended.
[00:35] Maya (LakeMed): sounds perfect. our main constraints: sub-200ms median token latency for short prompts, cost target ~ $0.0006 per token equivalent, and strict PHI handling — so private deployment might be needed.
[00:50] Priya (LakeMed): and from ops, we need SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management.
[00:58] Sara: noted. we'll cover SOC2 and KMS and how private deployments integrate with customer KMS. okay daniel, over to you — demo time.

[01:10] Daniel: pulling up the console now. first screen is the model catalog — we surface curated open models along with verified perf profiles. you'll see filters: task (chat/generation/embedding), architecture, quantization (FP16, int8, q4x, etc.), and recommended usage patterns.
[01:30] Daniel: i'll click on an open chat model — the profile shows throughput numbers (tokens/sec), median latency at different seq lengths, and a benchmark tab where we ran real workload sims. note these are per our lab infra, your numbers will depend on payload, batch size, and routing.
[01:50] Jared: quick q — these benchmarks, are they on A100s or a mixture?
[01:55] Daniel: good q. we include per-kernel numbers for both A100 and H100, plus CPU fallback numbers. the compatibility matrix maps model variants to recommended instance types and quantization profiles. for example, an int8 quant on H100 gives a 1.6x throughput improvement vs FP16 on A100 in our tests.
[02:20] Maya: can you show the compatibility matrix?
[02:25] Daniel: sure — here it is, matrix rows are model families, columns are hw + quantization. each cell has a green/yellow/red indicator for recommended production use and a popover with latency/cost estimates, known caveats (kv cache implications), and notes about quantization fidelity.
[02:45] Priya: kv cache spelling — sometimes the transcript shows K V cache — is that something that impacts memory?
[02:50] Daniel: yeah, KV cache management is important; when you use large context windows, the cache grows and affects per-seq memory. the matrix flags models that are cache-friendly vs those that need chunking.

[03:10] Daniel: back to model selection — we recommend starting with one of the verified open chat models (we show top-3 by cost/quality tradeoff). you can also pin to a specific model version in the API or console for rollouts.
[03:30] Sara: an example workflow — choose a model in the catalog, run a small synthetic benchmark from our UI (or API) against your prompt set, review quality and latency curves, then decide hosted POC vs Dedicated reserved capacity.
[03:47] Jared: for PHI, we assume private deploy — can Redwood run the private control plane in our VPC?
[03:54] Daniel: yes. private deployment options include VPC peering or fully on-prem package. we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and provide audit logs to your SIEM. SOC2 compliance docs are available — sara will share a packet.
[04:10] Maya: on quality, how do you measure regression risk when switching quant profiles?
[04:15] Daniel: we run evals tied to prompt sets — per-model regressions are tracked in the console; there's a quality delta metric and example failure cases. early in a rollout, we recommend A/B testing with a canary traffic split.
[04:30] Priya: show us the API for selecting model variants programmatically?
[04:35] Daniel: yes — in the API call you pass model_id and variant_id. we also have routing policies — latency_preferred vs cost_preferred — that'll automatically pick compatible variants or fallback models if capacity is constrained.
[04:55] Jared: any hard numbers for latency at our target 200ms token SLO?
[05:00] Daniel: rough rules — for single-token response rt, small open chat models on H100 with int8 quant hit ~80-120ms median under light load, on A100 closer to 120-180ms. your end-to-end will add network + pre/post processing. our bench sheets (i'll share) show per-model p50/p90 for 1-token and 64-token seqs.
[05:30] Maya: curious about batching — we need low latency but want cost efficiency. how does Redwood balance that?
[05:37] Daniel: continuous batching adapts to traffic. for latency-sensitive routes you can set max_batch_ms to keep latency tight; Optimize suggests batching/caching configs based on observed traffic to reduce per-token cost while honoring SLOs.
[05:55] Sara: i'll show the Optimize tab quickly — it surfaces suggested quant settings and batching that meet declared SLOs. the tool will say e.g., try q4x on this model with max_batch_ms 8ms, expected cost delta -18% and p95 latency +12ms.

[06:20] Jared: for the POC, we want to run our prompt set and compare 3 model variants. timeline?
[06:26] Sara: typical POC 2-3 weeks: week 1 onboarding + data, week 2 bench runs + quality evals, week 3 tuning and handoff. for a deeper integration we can do a 6-week pilot.
[06:40] Maya: okay, good. about data persistence — does Redwood keep transcripts? retention policies?
[06:45] Daniel: by default hosted keeps minimal logs for troubleshooting, but for enterprise you can configure no retention or forward logs to your S3. Private deployments give you full control. we also do field-level pseudonymization if required.
[07:05] Priya: SSO / SAML — any gaps?
[07:08] Sara: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and granular route permissions. we'll send SSO setup docs.

[07:30] (demo continues — Daniel steps through a sample benchmark run)
[08:00] Daniel: here's the benchmark run UI — you upload prompts or drop a CSV. I'm running a synthetic batch for the triage flows now. you'll see p50/p90/p99 and a token-cost column panned across model variants.
[09:15] Jared: I see a model called 'open-chat-l2' labeled green but quality note says 'hallucination risk on long-context medical phrasing' — how should we treat that?
[09:25] Daniel: yep, we flag domain-specific failure modes. for medical phrasing we'd recommend either a model with instruction tuning for clinical data or a hybrid approach: use an embedding + retrieval step for factual grounding and a smaller chat model for generation.
[09:45] Maya: do you have benchmark examples wit real medical prompts?
[09:49] Daniel: in some of our customer benchmarks, yes — we can share an anonymized sheet. for the POC, please share 200-300 real prompts and we'll run them through candidate models.
[10:05] Sara: quick pause for logistics — i'll follow up with pricing tiers: hosted per-token rates, dedicated reserved pricing, and private licensing.
[10:15] Jared: and SLA?
[10:17] Sara: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort SLAs but we have enterprise options with enhanced SLOs. we'll include specifics in the SOW.
[10:30] (transcript contains occasional small transcription errors, e.g., "H one hundred" instead of H100, "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache")

[22:00] (mid-call recap)
[22:05] Sara: ok recap: we showed model catalog, benchmarks, compat matrix, and Optimize suggestions. agreed POC: run your prompt set across three candidate models, we'll provide bench sheet and guided tuning. action items: sara send pricing and deck; daniel share bench CSV and compat matrix; maya provide prompts.

[35:00] Jared: one last question on cost — if we use dedicated reserved capacity with burst, how is overage billed?
[35:10] Daniel: overage is billed at a tiered rate; reserved commit covers baseline throughput and you get burst pools for spikes. we'll include a sample cost model in the pricing doc so you can model usage scenarios.
[36:00] Maya: can we get a short security questionnaire answered?
[36:05] Sara: yes — we have an 8-10 page security questionnaire and SOC2 docs that i'll attach.

[40:00] Sara: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed POC dates. any last items?
[40:10] Priya: none here.
[40:12] Maya: thanks, looking forward.
[40:15] Jared: thanks all.
[40:20] Sara: great, talk soon. bye.

References / Links mentioned: model-catalog-deck.pdf (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/model-catalog-deck.pdf), benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/lakemed-bench.xlsx), SOC2-package.pdf (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-package.pdf).

End of transcript.
